rationale: C03 supplies an unmistakable two-paragraph drafting template for the child. Both first designate named agencies under section 103(a) because their functions have a direct and immediate connection with national defense and place them within the definition of “Department” for Title I; both then apply Title I to the agencies’ contracts and related subcontracts for amounts received or accrued after a specified effective date, regardless of when the contracts were made. The child principally substitutes the Bonneville Power Administration and a new effective date while making grammatical changes for a single agency. C22 is a slightly earlier instance of substantially the same template. C04 is related to one agency named in C03 but does not closely supply the child’s two-provision form.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Bonneville Power Administration, which exercises functions having a direct and immediate connection with the national defense, is hereby designated, pursuant to subsection (a) of section 103 of the Act, as an agency coming within the definition of the term "Department" for the purposes of Title I of the Act.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Defense Materials Procurement Agency, the Bureau of Mines, and the (United States) Geological Survey, each of which exercises functions having a direct and immediate connection with the national defense, are hereby designated, pursuant to section 103(a) of the Act, as agencies of the Government included within the definition of the term "Department" for the purposes of Title I of the Act.
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves the distinctive designation formula, statutory reference, national-defense finding, and defined-term consequence, changing chiefly the named agency and singular grammar.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In accordance with section 102 of the Act, the provisions of Title I of the Act shall be applicable to all contracts with the Bonneville Power Administration, and related subcontracts, to the extent of the amounts received or accrued on or after the first day of November, 1951, whether such contracts or subcontracts were made on, before, or after that date.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In accordance with section 102 of the Act, the provisions of Title I of the Act shall be applicable to all contracts with the Defense Materials Procurement Agency, the Bureau of Mines, and the (United States) Geological Survey, respectively, and related subcontracts, to the extent of the amounts received or accrued by a contractor or subcontractor on or after the first day of October 1951, whether such contracts or subcontracts were made on, before, or after that date.
shared_material.explanation: The second operative paragraph follows the same sequence and nearly identical language, with substitutions for the agency list and effective date.
